pr_title: [Merged by Bors] - Reuse texture when resolving multiple passes
pr_body:
# Objective

Fixes https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/issues/3499

## Solution

Uses a `HashMap` from `RenderTarget` to sampled textures when preparing `ViewTarget`s to ensure that two passes with the same render target get sampled to the same texture.

This builds on and depends on https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/pull/3412, so this will be a draft PR until #3412 is merged. All changes for this PR are in the last commit.
pr_comments: It looks like the depth buffer is also not being shared by passes.
As #3412 was merged, could you update this on top of main so we can get it reviewed and merged?
Sorry for the delay on this. This seems relatively uncontroversial / worth including in 0.7. I'll try to give it a proper review before release.

issue_context.title: Rendering two 3d passes to the same window only shows the last pass when MSAA is enabled
issue_context.body:
## Bevy version

https://github.com/HackerFoo/bevy/tree/two_passes_main

## Operating system & version

MacOS 12.1

## What you did

This will show a red and a green cube spinning:

    cargo run --example two_passes

Setting the MSAA samples to 4 will only show one cube.
comments: It looks like the clear pass is creating two separate attachments that are being fed through the two passes in parallel instead of combining them when using MSAA. This doesn't happen when MSAA is disabled. From the Metal debugger:

The bug seems to be in how the resolve textures are handled; the same texture should be used for both passes. Changing the test on this line to `true` gives the intended behavior: https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/main/crates/bevy_render/src/texture/texture_cache.rs#L44
@HackerFoo can this be closed since the camera-driven rendering PR was merged? I don't remember if it addressed MSAA or not.
Does MSAA work with multiple passes on main?

> Does MSAA work with multiple passes on main?

It does, but it isn't configurable per-pass yet (still a global). Given that this issue isn't talking about that, I think we can close it.

review_comments: Please update the preceding comment and explain why the depth buffer is being written to as it isn't obvious from this code alone, and Xcode will likely warn about it as wasted bandwidth usage so people may come here and want to change it. If there is a comment explaining why it is being written, then we can hopefully avoid some ping-ponging. :)
Done. I also filed #4174 as a reminder to remove the workaround after the issue is resolved.
Please include a URL link here: it's much more convenient.
